title: Split hot-path KV-read adapter; introduce ephemeral lease cache and scheduler watermark smoothing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: This ticket deconflates the KV read hot-path by extracting a lightweight KV-read adapter that serves two runtime callers: the continuous-batcher fast path and the session-lease reconciler. As part of the extraction we will add an ephemeral in-memory lease cache (bounded LRU) to reduce repeated cross-shard lookups and introduce a small scheduler watermark smoothing component to prevent micro-bursts from thrashing admission and slot allocation. The goal is to reduce p95 tail latency on short-sequence inferences and lower KV shard read amplification under high-concurrency workloads.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New KV-read adapter compiled behind a feature-flag and exercised in dogfood.
2) Ephemeral lease cache reduces remote shard read rate by >=25% under the synthetic small-seq workload (see benchmark harness).
3) P95 tail latency improvement of >=12% and p99 improvement of >=8% for <64-token requests measured in the canary cluster.
4) No increase in error rates or stale-lease regressions during a 72-hour canary.
5) Rolling disable path present and tested to ensure safe rollback.
implementation_notes:
- Introduce kv_read_adapter::FastRead and kv_read_adapter::SafeRead interfaces.
- FastRead is lock-free and uses preallocated read buffers; SafeRead falls back to existing sharded lookup logic.
- EphemeralLeaseCache: small LRU with ~1024 entries by default, TTL tunable per-tenant, metrics exported: lease_cache.hit, lease_cache.miss, lease_cache.evictions.
- Scheduler watermark smoother: moving-median window (configurable 250ms) applied to admission token bucket signals to avoid admission oscillation.
- Feature flag: ff.runtime.kv_adapter_split (default off).
- Add unit tests for adapter invariants and eviction behavior.
- Add integration test in runtime-qa harness that simulates hot-key churn and verifies reduced cross-shard reads.
- Coordinate with infra to reserve a canary slice for two weeks.
telemetry_and_benchmarks:
Bench harness: tools/benchmarks/kv-hotpath-smallseq.
Baseline: canary-2025-02: smallseq p95=34ms, p99=89ms, remote-kv-reads=8200 RPS per shard.
Target after change: p95<=30ms, remote-kv-reads<=6150 RPS.
Key metrics to publish in console: batch_latency.p50/p95/p99, kv_reads.remote.rate, lease_cache.hit_ratio, admission.retries.
Initial local microbench: FastRead single-threaded latency 1.8us vs legacy 5.6us for cached-path.
Will run full cluster load tests during canary windows and capture flamegraphs for any regression.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge behind flag and run non-production cluster for 48h.
2) Enable flag for 10% traffic on canary slice (observe 24h).
3) Increase to 40% if stable (observe 48h).
4) Full canary for 72h; if metrics pass, schedule 2-hour rolling release to production.
5) Post-release checklist: watch for lease-staleness alerts for 24h and eviction spike anomalies.
Rollback: feature-flag off and revert admission smoothing within 30 minutes if severe regressions occur.
test_plan:
- Unit: adapter behavior, eviction boundary, TTL expiry, metrics emission.
- Integration: runtime-qa scenario 'hotkey-churn' with and without adapter.
- Stress: 24h soak at peak QPS of customer-simulated work.
- Chaos: simulate delayed shard responses and validate SafeRead fallback triggers correctly.
- Regression: run existing perf benchmark suite and compare against baseline artifacts.
- Acceptance: metrics assertions automated in canary pipeline.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: lease cache could serve stale leases leading to incorrect routing. Mitigation: short default TTL (100ms), SafeRead fallback, and instrumentation to track any lease_mismatch events.
Risk: admission smoothing may underutilize burst capacity. Mitigation: conservative default smoothing window and ability to tune per-cluster.
Risk: micro-optimizations introduce memory pressure under tens of thousands of tenants. Mitigation: bounded cache per-shard and aggregate memory gauges.
Risk: compilation or dependency churn. Mitigation: land in a feature branch and run full integration pipeline; coordinate with infra to pin runtime dep versions.
